nik: quick RFC follow-up  we need a crisp boundary between SLA-weighted admission and burst admission. propose a tiny policy evaluator that enforces SLA bands and delegates capacity changes to the existing autoscaler.
maria: thin evaluator = admission gate + counters only? dont want another control loop.
sam: agree. model SLA band as per-tenant token bucket so runtime logic stays simple.
lee: when tokens drain, tenants want different behaviors: reject (with retry guidance) or fallback to cheaper model variants. both should be tenant-configurable.
nik: example policy (human readable): sla_weight:0.75, token_capacity:1200, refill_per_min:400, fallbacks:[gptx-s-8q,gptx-2b-int8]. also consider adaptive refill based on observed p95 with EWMA smoothing.
maria: adaptive refill ok but add min floor to avoid oscillation.
sam: control-plane proxy seems like the right home: dry-run rollout, audit logs, easier HA.
lee: ops need signals: emit "sla_band_depleted" events and metric tags (tenant_id, action).
infra-bot: deploy note: autoscaler-proxy v0.9 canaryed in cluster-b.
nik: testing: build simulation harness that replays recent traces and outputs csv of rejections, fallback_calls, tokens_used, estimated_cost_delta. evaluator must be pure so dry-run equals live.
maria: I can own the sim harness and push a first PR this week.
sam: I'll prototype proxy API + policy YAML schema.
lee: I'll spec metrics and 429 payload (Retry-After + X-Redwood-Fallback-URL) and mock dashboard.
nik: logging: publish ndjson decisions to kafka topic sla-policy-decisions.v1. infra confirmed topic.
infra-bot: notice: topic sla-policy-decisions.v1 created (retention=14d).
nik: follow-ups: maria sim PR, sam proxy sketch, lee metrics PR. post links here when ready. thanks! :raised_hands:
